articles.title: Websites shut down globally after AI finds cybersecurity flaw affecting 70% of the internet
articles.summary: Government and company websites around the world briefly went dark and suspended some services, as operators scrambled to patch their systems after artificial intelligence helped find critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language.
articles.body: Government and company websites around the world briefly went dark and suspended some services, as operators scrambled to patch their systems after artificial intelligence helped find critical vulnerabilities in a widely used programming language. A UK government spokesperson told reporters Thursday that work was underway “across the government” to identify and fix potential vulnerabilities. “No large public-facing critical services are being affected by the exercise but some limited services may temporarily be offline while security work is carried out,” the spokesperson said. The US National Security Agency and Europe’s cybersecurity agency have advised companies to take immediate action to address two critical flaws in PHP, a programming language that powers 70% of all websites in the world, including WordPress and Drupal, an open-source content management system. The PHP Foundation, the organization behind the coding language, has released a patch for the bugs, which have been hidden in their software for years, and is urging website operators to update their systems immediately. Popular Irish news website The Journal was temporarily offline Thursday morning while it bolstered its “defences,” it said in a notice. The Journal is Ireland’s second most-used online news source, behind only RTÉ, the national broadcaster, according to the Reuters Institute. The flaws in PHP – which originally stood for Personal Home Page – were uncovered by teams at OpenAI, Google-owned cybersecurity company Wiz, and another cybersecurity company, Calif. The bugs, collectively called PHP2Shell, could allow attackers to hack into websites and read memory that could contain sensitive information, like passwords. “With PHP behind such a vast share of the web, the exposure could reach almost everywhere people spend money online,” said Nigel Green, the CEO of deVere Group, a financial advisory firm. “Booking platforms, marketplaces, subscription services, ticketing sites, delivery apps and utility portals could all be holding card details on systems built with the same kind of code,” he added. World leaders weigh in Even world leaders urged organizations to take action. Dutch Prime Minister Rob Jetten said that his cabinet was “closely monitoring the situation surrounding the vulnerabilities in PHP.” Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said companies should consider suspending services if necessary in order to reduce their exposure. “Please check if your publicly available websites use PHP, and prepare to apply the fix patch that will be released tonight… as soon as possible,” she posted on X Wednesday. Japanese airline ANA, railway operator JR West and the country’s largest bank, MUFG, were among companies that reported some webpages and services temporarily suspended. In Europe, government websites in France, Denmark, Finland and the Netherlands, including the Dutch cyber security agency, were temporarily taken offline while security fixes were implemented. The Wikimedia Foundation, the non-profit that operates Wikipedia, told CNN Thursday that it was “in the process of addressing security vulnerabilities in PHP,” and that a number of its systems had been taken down as a “precautionary measure.” ‘AI inflection point’ AI played a crucial role in finding and fixing vulnerabilities “that had remained hidden in the PHP codebase for more than a decade,” according to Wiz, which said the episode marks an “AI inflection point.” “What AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit,” Wiz researchers wrote in a blog post Wednesday in which they described PHP as a “backbone of the web.” “With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work,” they added. The bugs were discovered in late August but were disclosed to the public only on Wednesday, after PHP had come up with a fix. The flaws could allow attackers to remotely execute code, disrupt services and expose customer data, according to web infrastructure provider Cloudflare, which has been working with the PHP Foundation, Calif, OpenAI and Wiz to address the issue. Researchers at Wiz used Google’s Gemini 4 Argon, Wiz Atlas and OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol during the research process. Heartbleed similarities Wiz researchers say the issue is on par with the Heartbleed bug from 2014, which impacted an encryption technology estimated to be used by two-thirds of the Web. Heartbleed allowed cybercriminals to access data that should have been protected. Like Heartbleed, the researchers at Wiz say PHP2Shell could similarly serve as a turning point in cybersecurity. While the vulnerabilities existed for years, AI made it practical to deploy them. “The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” the researchers said. “Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit.” – CNN’s John Liu, Anna Cooban, Amy Croffey and James Frater contributed reporting.

articles.title: Delta Electronics starts CCTV production with its subsidiary Vivotek
articles.summary: Delta Electronics India begins manufacturing Vivotek smart CCTV cameras at its Krishnagiri plant, starting with BIS-compliant commercial models and scaling AI models.
articles.body: Chennai: Delta Electronics India has begun producing smart surveillance cameras with its digital security system subsidiary VIVOTEK at its Krishnagiri plant in Tamil Nadu.Initial manufacturing will focus on the commercial series compliant with India’s mandatory BIS standards, while VIVOTEK plans to widen its portfolio by phasing in mid-to-high-end AI surveillance models tailored for smart cities and intelligent transportation systems (ITS). Delta will scale up Krishnagiri’s manufacturing capacity, the company said in a statement.India has effectively restricted China-made CCTVs, opening opportunities for domestic manufacturing. Local production significantly cuts spare-parts turnaround times, enabling system integrators to meet domestic procurement criteria and compete in government and public tenders, it said. articles.title: Veja as propostas de Lula e Flávio para o seu bolso | G1
articles.standfirst: Compare os planos de governo dos candidatos para salário, emprego, impostos, benefícios, aposentadoria, crédito e moradia, de acordo com o seu perfil.
articles.summary: Compare os planos de governo dos candidatos para salário, emprego, impostos, benefícios, aposentadoria, crédito e moradia, de acordo com o seu perfil.
articles.body:
Lula (à esq) e Flávio Bolsonaro (à dir) participaram de sabatinas na TV Globo — Foto: Divulgação

Os planos de governo de Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva ( PT ) e Flávio Bolsonaro ( PL ) para a Presidência da República trazem diferentes diretrizes para temas estruturais do país.

Além de visões contrastantes sobre o papel do Estado na economia, os dois candidatos também apresentam caminhos diferentes para lidar com as contas públicas, o mercado de trabalho, a renda e a inflação.

No mercado de trabalho, por exemplo, os planos partem de estratégias diferentes: enquanto Lula concentra propostas na renda e na jornada de trabalho, Flávio Bolsonaro prioriza a redução do custo de contratação pelas empresas.

Já na economia, Lula dá mais peso à atuação do Estado, ao crédito e a políticas públicas, enquanto Flávio enfatiza equilíbrio fiscal, redução de tributos e de custos para empresas.

Entenda nesta reportagem quais propostas podem mexer com sua vida financeira, de acordo com o seu perfil.

⚠️ A comparação considera exclusivamente as propostas apresentadas nos planos de governo dos dois candidatos.

Lula : Promete manter a política de valorização do salário mínimo, com reajustes acima da inflação.

Flávio : Não apresenta fórmula de reajuste ou meta para o salário mínimo, mas defende que juros mais baixos e inflação controlada aumentariam o poder de compra das famílias.

Lula : Propõe rever regras trabalhistas que, segundo o plano, favorecem a precarização, combater fraudes em terceirizações e fortalecer a negociação coletiva. Também prevê retomar a participação dos sindicatos nas homologações de rescisões trabalhistas.

Flávio : Defende jornadas e horários flexíveis e a prevalência do negociado sobre o legislado, permitindo que acordos ou convenções coletivas prevaleçam sobre determinadas regras previstas na legislação trabalhista.

⚠️ O plano de Lula previa o fim da escala 6x1 e a redução da jornada para 40 horas semanais, sem redução salarial. Flávio, que inicialmente se posicionava contra a proposta e defendia um modelo mais flexível de jornada, mudou de posição e votou a favor da medida no Senado. A mudança foi aprovada pelo Congresso e promulgada neste mês.

Lula : Defende isenção total do IR para rendimentos mensais de até R$ 5 mil, com compensação por meio da tributação da renda dos mais ricos.

Flávio : Não propõe diretamente mudanças no Imposto de Renda da Pessoa Física, mas defende revisar e redimensionar a reforma tributária para reduzir a tributação sobre o consumo.

Lula : Defende retomar a participação obrigatória dos sindicatos nas rescisões trabalhistas.

Flávio : Defende manter facultativo o imposto sindical e reduzir a participação dos sindicatos nas negociações individuais entre trabalhadores e empresas.

Igualdade salarial e de acesso ao mercado de trabalho:

Lula : Propõe reforçar a aplicação da Lei de Igualdade Salarial entre homens e mulheres e combater discriminações no acesso ao trabalho, inclusive por raça, etnia, deficiência, orientação sexual, identidade de gênero e classe.

Flávio : Propõe programas gratuitos de capacitação e a criação de um banco nacional de vagas conectado às empresas para ampliar o acesso das mulheres ao mercado de trabalho. Também prevê criar a Central da Mulher, com acesso a vagas, orientação para empreender, crédito e renegociação de dívidas.

Carreiras e relações de trabalho no serviço público:

Lula : Propõe regulamentar o direito à negociação coletiva no setor público e ampliar o diálogo entre governo e servidores por meio da Mesa Nacional de Negociação Permanente. Também defende a valorização e a qualificação do funcionalismo.

Flávio : Propõe uma reforma administrativa, com mudanças na estrutura do Estado e nas carreiras dos servidores, sem detalhar quais regras pretende alterar.

Piso do Magistério e combate a supersalários:

Lula : Prevê manter o Piso Nacional do Magistério e apoiar a formação de docentes por meio de iniciativas como o Pé-de-Meia Licenciaturas e o Bolsa Mais Professores.

Flávio: Prevê combater supersalários e pagamentos adicionais, além de reduzir ministérios e cargos comissionados. Também propõe capacitação contínua de professores.

📱 Sou trabalhador por conta própria: autônomo, informal ou trabalhador por aplicativo

Lula : Defende regulamentar o trabalho em plataformas digitais, com regras sobre remuneração, condições de trabalho e direitos trabalhistas e previdenciários, além de transparência sobre decisões tomadas pelos algoritmos das plataformas, como critérios de bloqueio, taxas de comissão e distribuição de corridas.

Flávio : Defende manter as oportunidades de renda e trabalho geradas pelos aplicativos, mas não detalha como pretende fazer isso. Afirma que os trabalhadores terão proteção social e previdenciária e critica a participação dos sindicatos na definição das regras para o setor.

Lula : Propõe ampliar a proteção social de trabalhadores autônomos, com cobertura previdenciária e proteção em casos de acidentes, doenças e períodos sem trabalho. Também prevê formas mais flexíveis de contribuição à Previdência e maior fiscalização contra a pejotização irregular.

Flávio : Afirma que assegurará “efetiva proteção social e previdenciária” aos trabalhadores por aplicativo, mas não detalha um modelo previdenciário para os trabalhadores por conta própria em geral. Também propõe reduzir o custo da contratação com carteira assinada para estimular empregos formais.

💼 Tenho meu próprio negócio: MEIs, micro e pequenas empresas e empregadores no geral

Lula : Propõe ampliar o acesso de autônomos e pequenos negócios ao crédito, inclusive por meio de fundos garantidores, além de oferecer qualificação e assistência técnica. Também prevê facilitar o acesso a compras públicas e financiar ações de digitalização e aumento da produtividade.

Flávio : Propõe o Minha Primeira Empresa, com capacitação e orientação pelo Sistema S e acesso a crédito e serviços da Caixa. Também prevê crédito e orientação para pequenos negócios.

⚠️ Em 21 de outubro, Lula sancionou uma lei que perdoa a dívida de MEIs, amplia o limite de faturamento da categoria e permite a contratação de mais funcionários. Saiba mais.

Burocracia, impostos e regras para empresas:

Lula : Propõe simplificar o ambiente de negócios e assegurar tratamento tributário específico às pequenas empresas durante a implementação da reforma tributária.

Flávio : Propõe ampliar as medidas da Lei de Liberdade Econômica, simplificando registros, licenças e outros procedimentos para abrir e manter empresas. Também prevê revisar normas consideradas obsoletas e reduzir tributos sobre a produção.

Lula : Defende associar políticas de crédito público, assistência técnica, incentivos fiscais e compras governamentais à geração de empregos. Também prevê estimular oportunidades de trabalho em áreas de interesse coletivo, como conservação ambiental, cultura, esporte e economia do cuidado.

Flávio : Propõe reduzir gradualmente o custo da contratação formal, sem retirar direitos, para estimular a criação de empregos com carteira assinada.

Primeiro emprego e recolocação profissional:

Lula : Propõe ampliar políticas de qualificação e inserção profissional, inclusive para trabalhadores afetados pelas transformações tecnológicas e pessoas com mais de 60 anos. Também prevê ampliar, na rede Sine, uma plataforma que reúna vagas, cursos, certificações e orientação profissional.

Flávio : Propõe contratos com menor custo de contratação para jovens de 18 a 24 anos em busca do primeiro emprego e para pessoas com 50 anos ou mais desempregadas há pelo menos 12 meses. Também prevê criar um banco nacional de vagas conectado às áreas de RH das empresas para aproximar candidatos e empregadores.

Lula : Propõe aprimorar o Pé-de-Meia e ampliar a assistência estudantil no ensino superior, incluindo alimentação e moradia. Também prevê manter os investimentos em cursinhos populares e continuar expandindo a rede de institutos federais.

Flávio : Propõe substituir o atual modelo de financiamento estudantil por um empréstimo em que o estudante só começaria a pagar após conseguir emprego e renda. As parcelas seriam proporcionais ao salário, com prazo mais longo para pagamento. Também prevê remunerar estudantes com bom desempenho que ofereçam reforço escolar a colegas com dificuldades.

Reajuste dos benefícios e salário mínimo:

Lula : Propõe concluir a modernização e o aprimoramento dos serviços previdenciários e continuar reduzindo o tempo de espera pela concessão de benefícios do INSS.

Flávio : Propõe digitalizar processos e profissionalizar a gestão do INSS para reduzir a fila. Também prevê um novo pacote antifraude e mudanças no consignado, com dupla checagem para evitar descontos não autorizados.

Saúde, medicamentos e cuidados na velhice:

Lula : Defende manter o Farmácia Popular, com revisão dos produtos oferecidos gratuitamente e ampliação dos locais de retirada, além da inclusão de exames laboratoriais e de acompanhamento de doenças crônicas. Para os idosos, propõe ampliar Centros-Dia, vagas públicas em instituições de longa permanência e atendimento domiciliar.

Flávio : Propõe entregar medicamentos em domicílio a idosos, pessoas com deficiência e doentes crônicos e criar uma Rede Nacional de Cuidado, com centros-dia e atendimento domiciliar. Também prevê subsídios para adaptações de acessibilidade na casa de famílias de baixa renda e a ampliação de instituições de longa permanência para idosos.

Benefícios sociais e acesso ao trabalho:

Lula : Propõe fortalecer a proteção social, com mais recursos e expansão e modernização da rede de atendimento. Também prevê ampliar políticas de enfrentamento da pobreza infantil e de acesso a serviços públicos.

Flávio : Propõe manter os programas sociais existentes, aperfeiçoar a gestão, corrigir distorções e combater fraudes. Também prevê dar prioridade aos beneficiários em ações voltadas ao mercado de trabalho e permitir o retorno imediato ao benefício após o seguro-desemprego, mantidos os critérios de elegibilidade.

Lula : Propõe manter a inflação sob controle e criar condições para uma redução sustentada dos juros, com responsabilidade fiscal. Também prevê buscar o barateamento da energia elétrica e reduzir os efeitos da volatilidade dos preços internacionais sobre os combustíveis.

Flávio : Propõe buscar equilíbrio fiscal e superávits primários, medidas que, segundo o plano, contribuiriam para reduzir a inflação e os juros. Também prevê reduzir impostos sobre energia elétrica e combustíveis e encargos da conta de luz, mantendo a tarifa social.

Lula : Propõe continuar monitorando o endividamento das famílias, manter mecanismos de controle de gastos excessivos com apostas on-line e aprimorar as regras de oferta e concessão de crédito, ampliando a proteção ao consumidor.

Flávio : Propõe reduzir os juros e o custo do crédito por meio do equilíbrio fiscal e da redução da dívida pública. Para as mulheres, prevê programas de orientação financeira sobre orçamento doméstico, endividamento e formação de poupança.

Lula : Propõe ampliar o apoio a estados e municípios para expandir a educação infantil e fortalecer a Política Nacional de Cuidados. Também prevê apoiar Cuidotecas e estruturas como lavanderias públicas, cozinhas solidárias e restaurantes populares, além de criar um programa de capacitação de cuidadores.

Flávio : Propõe ampliar a oferta de creches em período integral e oferecer vouchers para acesso à rede privada credenciada onde não houver vaga pública. Também prevê criar uma Rede Nacional de Cuidado, com centros-dia e atendimento domiciliar para idosos e pessoas com deficiência.

Lula : Propõe ampliar os recursos do Plano Safra e manter juros compatíveis com a atividade agropecuária, com prioridade para investimentos em máquinas e tecnologias. Para a agricultura familiar, prevê ampliar o crédito, priorizar a produção de alimentos da cesta básica e simplificar o acesso aos recursos.

Flávio : Prevê facilitar o acesso ao crédito pelo pequeno produtor por meio da regularização e titulação das propriedades, mas não detalha uma política específica de ampliação do crédito rural.

Lula : Promete fortalecer o seguro rural e, para a agricultura familiar, ampliar o acesso ao seguro e reforçar o Garantia-Safra. Também propõe discutir um instrumento para cobrir perdas decorrentes de quebras severas de safra.

Flávio : Propõe ampliar o seguro rural e criar ferramentas de securitização e reorganização das dívidas do setor, para dar maior previsibilidade financeira ao produtor.

Lula : Propõe ampliar o acesso ao crédito fundiário e avançar na regularização e titulação de terras. Também prevê acelerar a titulação de territórios quilombolas e a regularização fundiária de povos e comunidades tradicionais.

Flávio : Propõe acelerar a regularização fundiária e a titulação do pequeno proprietário rural para facilitar o acesso ao crédito e aos investimentos, além de reforçar a segurança jurídica do direito de propriedade.

Lula : Propõe acelerar a produção nacional de fertilizantes e fomentar a produção de bioinsumos para reduzir a dependência de produtos importados.

Flávio : Propõe apoiar a produção nacional de fertilizantes, aproveitando reservas brasileiras de minerais como potássio e fosfato e incentivando a produção a partir do gás, para reduzir a dependência externa.

Programas habitacionais e financiamento:

Lula : Propõe manter e ampliar o Minha Casa, Minha Vida para todas as faixas de renda, com foco nas famílias de menor renda. Também prevê fortalecer o Compra Assistida para a aquisição de imóveis prontos.

Flávio : Propõe retomar o Casa Verde e Amarela, com meta de 2,5 milhões de moradias e financiamento a juros mais baixos.

Lula : Promete assegurar recursos para concluir obras de urbanização e regularização fundiária em favelas e periferias e apoiar novos projetos. Também prevê destinar imóveis e terrenos da União à regularização de moradias de famílias que já vivem nesses locais.

Flávio : Propõe incentivar a regularização fundiária, priorizando áreas urbanas já consolidadas, para que famílias que vivem nesses locais obtenham a escritura do imóvel. O plano prevê dar preferência à escritura em nome da mulher.

articles.title: Abóbora de 1.500 kg bate recorde mundial e entra para o Guinness | G1
articles.standfirst: O agricultor recebeu US$ 3.500 pela vitória em competição local, o equivalente a cerca de R$ 17.599. Já é a terceira vez que ele entra para o livro dos recordes com o plantio.
articles.summary: O agricultor recebeu US$ 3.500 pela vitória em competição local, o equivalente a cerca de R$ 17.599. Já é a terceira vez que ele entra para o Guinness com o plantio.
articles.body:
Uma abóbora de 1.432 kg colhida nos Estados Unidos bateu o recorde mundial de peso e foi reconhecida pelo Guinness World Records.

Ela foi cultivada pelo produtor rural Ron Wallace, do estado de Rhode Island, e pesada no dia 10 de outubro durante um concurso de abóboras gigantes realizado no sul da região da Nova Inglaterra, nos EUA.

O título foi oficializado no dia 14 de outubro. O recorde até então pertencia a uma abóbora de 1.296 kg cultivada por Ian Paton, de Lymington, na Inglaterra . A marca havia sido estabelecida em 3 de outubro — uma semana antes da pesagem da abóbora americana.

Segundo o Guinness, é quase inédito que o recorde nessa categoria troque de mãos tão rápido. A única outra ocasião em que isso aconteceu foi em 2 de outubro de 1999, quando o recorde foi estabelecido duas vezes no mesmo dia.

A abóbora é a primeira da história a ultrapassar a marca de 1.360 kg e poderia render mais de três mil tortas.

Segundo a agência de notícias Associated Press, Wallace recebeu US$ 3.500 pela vitória na competição local, o equivalente a cerca de R$ 17.599.

O produtor contou que organizadores de outros concursos tentaram atraí-lo com prêmios maiores, alguns de até US$ 70 mil, mas que, para ele, era importante estar cercado pelas pessoas de sua comunidade no momento da vitória histórica.

Abóbora gigante de 1.432 quilos colhida nos EUA pode bater recorde mundial — Foto: Reprodução

Wallace atribui parte do resultado à troca de dicas e técnicas entre os produtores de abóboras gigantes. Neste ano, pela primeira vez, ele passou a cultivá-las em uma estufa, o que, segundo o agricultor, fez uma grande diferença.

“Este foi meu primeiro ano cultivando em estufa e o clima esteve quase perfeito durante a maior parte da temporada. [Mas na hora da pesagem], eu estava exausto”, declarou Wallace ao Guinness World Records.

Ele começou a cultivar abóboras por hobby há 35 anos, inspirado por seu pai, a quem reconhece como "um dos primeiros cultivadores de abóboras gigantes na Nova Inglaterra".

Para Wallace, as competições ajudam a valorizar o trabalho dos produtores, que têm sido cada vez mais procurados pelo setor agrícola para orientar sobre o manejo do solo e outras técnicas de cultivo.

Ron Wallace comemorando o peso da abóbora — Foto: Divulgação

O agricultor já é veterano nos recordes do Guinness com abóboras. A primeira vez aconteceu em 2006, com um fruto de 681,3 kg.

Wallace com sua primeira abóbora recordista mundial em 2006. — Foto: Divulgação

Em 2012, ele repetiu o feito. Dessa vez, a abóbora alcançou 911,27 kg.

Wallace com sua segunda abóbora recordista mundial ainda no pé, em 2012. — Foto: Divulgação

"Meus dois recordes mundiais anteriores foram conquistas históricas na época, mas este tem um significado ainda mais especial. Tive alguns anos de dificuldade no cultivo, pois estava adotando uma abordagem mais científica. Foi ótimo ver tudo se concretizar!", disse o produtor ao Guinness World Records.

articles.title: A majority of Americans have low-quality jobs
articles.summary: Only about four in 10 American workers say that they have a decent job, finds a new survey on job quality from Gallup out Thursday.
articles.body:
Only about four in 10 American workers say that they have a decent job, finds a new survey on job quality from Gallup out Thursday.

Why it matters: Bad jobs aren't just a misery for employees — for companies, they're linked to costly turnover and higher health care expenses.

Zoom in: Gallup defines a quality job as one that meets minimum standards across a few dimensions: fair pay and benefits; a safe and respectful workplace free from harassment and discrimination; and a predictable schedule.

Gallup surveyed 17,874 employed adults ages 18 to 75 from Jan. 26 - March 24.

By the numbers: This year, 41% of workers meet Gallup's standards for a quality job, unchanged from 2025.

Older workers and those with advanced degrees are more likely to have a good job.

Those with low-quality jobs were nearly twice as likely to work for a different employer after one year.

And 51% of those with higher-quality jobs report better health, compared with 35% in non-quality jobs.

The big picture: This is the second year the Gallup, Jobs for the Future and The Families and Workers Fund has released its American Job Quality study and it comes at a turbulent time for workers.

While at a high level, the labor market looks good — with low unemployment and few layoffs — hiring rates are down. If you don't have a job, it's hard to land one, a particularly vexing problem for new grads.

Between the lines: This is partly an AI issue.

A good number of employers are looking to see if they can do more with fewer workers, as they incorporate AI into their workflows, HR executives and workplace experts said at an event hosted by Charter this week.

The twist: AI use is more common in the better jobs typically held by college grads, per Gallup. Those are the workers stressed that AI will replace them.

The bottom line: Most Americans are working in low-quality jobs — and those with a good job worry about AI taking it away.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Rupee weakened in early trade on Thursday, losing 12 paise to 94.50 against the US dollar as rising crude oil prices and a decline in the equity market weighed down the currency. A softer dollar and lower US treasury yields, however, helped limit the fall.The currency opened at 94.47 at the interbank foreign exchange market before slipping to 94.50. The decline came a day after the rupee had climbed 53 paise to close at 94.38 against the dollar on Wednesday.Forex analysts said the rupee was trading on a flat-to-lower note amid pressure from the domestic stock market and higher oil prices. articles.title: Compra dos jarrones por 20 euros en una tienda benéfica de Londres y descubre que valen más de 68.000 euros
articles.standfirst: El coleccionista adquirió las piezas sin conocer su origen
articles.summary: El coleccionista adquirió las piezas sin conocer su origen
articles.body: A veces, los mayores tesoros aparecen donde menos se esperan. Eso fue lo que le ocurrió a un coleccionista que encontró dos jarrones de colores en una tienda benéfica de Londres. Pagó alrededor de 20 libras por ambos, unos 24 euros, sin imaginar que aquellas piezas acabarían protagonizando una subasta por una cantidad miles de veces superior a su precio original. Los objetos, que a primera vista podían pasar por simples adornos, llamaron su atención por sus características y las marcas que presentaban en la base. Tras investigar su posible procedencia, decidió recurrir a especialistas para conocer su verdadero valor. El resultado confirmó que no se trataba de cerámica corriente, sino de dos piezas de porcelana china del siglo XVIII vinculadas a la dinastía Qing. Los dos recipientes, de aproximadamente 11,4 centímetros de altura, destacan por su decoración floral. Sobre un fondo amarillo aparecen crisantemos rojos y amarillos, acompañados de motivos de flores de loto y hojas verdes. Su elaboración responde a la técnica tradicional china doucai, que combina pintura azul bajo el esmalte con otros colores aplicados posteriormente. Las piezas fueron fabricadas en Jingdezhen, una localidad de la provincia china de Jiangxi conocida históricamente por su producción de porcelana. En sus bases aparecen marcas asociadas al emperador Qianlong, que gobernó entre 1735 y 1796 y cuyo reinado estuvo estrechamente ligado a las artes y a la producción de objetos destinados a la corte imperial. La pareja salió a subasta en Roseberys, una casa especializada en arte y antigüedades de Londres, en mayo de 2023. La venta alcanzó las 58.000 libras, incluidos los gastos correspondientes al comprador, una cifra superior a los 74.000 dólares. El resultado convirtió una adquisición aparentemente insignificante en un hallazgo extraordinario. Pese a presentar algunos desperfectos, como pequeñas grietas y arañazos, las piezas despertaron un notable interés por su antigüedad, su decoración y su relación con la porcelana imperial china. El caso demuestra hasta qué punto la experiencia de los especialistas puede resultar determinante en el mercado de las antigüedades: objetos que pasan inadvertidos en establecimientos de segunda mano pueden esconder un valor histórico y económico excepcional.

articles.title: Tesla reports $1.53 billion in free cash flow amid one-fifth cut to 2026 spending forecast
articles.summary: Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent
articles.body: Tesla reported an unexpected $1.53 billion in free cash flow in the third quarter, beating Wall Street's expectations, as the electric vehicle maker spent less than anticipated on capital expenditure.However, a one-fifth cut to its 2026 spending forecast has raised questions about its investment plans for artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and autonomous driving. The company now expects capital expenditure of around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not specify which areas would see lower spending.In the quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent a year earlier but well below the $7.5 billion analysts had expected on average, according to LSEG data.The lower spending helped Tesla report free cash flow of $1.53 billion, compared with market expectations of a cash outflow of $4.92 billion.Tesla's shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the results, supported by positive free cash flow, higher gross margins and revenue that exceeded Wall Street expectations. However, the stock reversed direction to trade 2% lower. Shares have fallen around 14% this year."The free cash flow beat was a pleasant surprise, but when combined with the lower-than-expected capex, raises questions on the next step for the automaker," said Ryan Lee, senior vice president of product and strategy at Direxion, which offers exchange-traded funds tied to Tesla. "Lower capex suggests less of an 'all-in' approach to the AI arms race than one would expect from Elon."SpaceX merger puts Tesla's spending under scrutinyThe results come as chief executive Elon Musk explores a potential combination of Tesla and SpaceX, his space venture. The unexpected cash generation could strengthen Tesla's financial position ahead of a possible deal, but lower investment in AI, robotaxis and humanoid robots could raise concerns about its ability to deliver on its growth ambitions.On Tuesday, Musk described a merger between the two companies as a "good idea" and said they had formed special committees to discuss the proposal. He declined to provide further details during Wednesday's conference call with analysts.A combination would bring together businesses central to Musk's long-term vision of an integrated technology and manufacturing group spanning AI, energy, robotics, communications and transportation on Earth and beyond.However, investors will want to see whether Tesla is investing enough to turn Musk's ambitions into commercial businesses, particularly as the robotaxi rollout has lagged behind his promises."The merger still faces a high bar, but tonight’s numbers make the financial logic harder to ignore," said Thomas Monteiro, a senior analyst at Investing.com."The main takeaway is that Tesla's surprisingly positive cash flow quarter did not come from stronger profits, but from spending billions less than planned at a time when SpaceX is preparing to invest up to $40 billion in a single quarter."Revenue beats estimates, but net income plunges 43%Tesla's financial performance presented a mixed picture. Revenue remained flat compared with a year earlier, despite the end of US tax credits that had supported sales in the previous year. Nevertheless, the figure exceeded Wall Street's expectations.Net income fell 43% during the quarter.Tesla said it had ended the quarter with its largest backlog of passenger vehicles in four years. Higher petrol prices have supported demand for electric vehicles, particularly in Europe.The company delivered 486,532 vehicles in the third quarter, putting it on track to increase annual deliveries for the first time in three years."Demand is growing rapidly for our vehicles. It's exceeding our production by a significant margin," Musk said on the conference call with analysts. "In a nutshell, after many years of sort of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we're now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth."FSD adoption and automotive margins improveTesla also reported stronger adoption of its driver-assistance technology in North America. The FSD (supervised) attach rate exceeded three-quarters of new vehicle deliveries, an increase of nearly 20 percentage points from the second quarter, the company said.Automotive gross margin, excluding regulatory credits, reached 18.1% in the third quarter, above analysts' estimate of 16.7%, according to Visible Alpha data.Tesla's energy business has recently helped offset pressures on its automotive operations. The latter remain under scrutiny as competitors worldwide launch newer, often cheaper models. Tesla continues to rely heavily on its ageing Model 3 and Model Y.Despite the competitive pressures, Tesla aims to produce five million vehicles annually by around 2030, compared with an expected 2.5 million this year.You use AI every day. articles.title: Ozempic wave boosts US cobblers and tailors as Americans tighten their belts
articles.summary: By Danielle Kaye and Alexander Marrow NEW YORK, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Lorraine Scott has spent at least $300 to tailor her pants and jeans since losing 60 pound...
articles.body:
NEW YORK, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Lorraine Scott has spent at least $300 to tailor her pants and jeans since losing 60 pounds on weight-loss drugs over the past year.

"Most of the things in my closet didn't fit anymore," she said. The 42-year-old Atlanta resident, who is known as ‌Lorraine Kamesha to her YouTube followers, has opted to alter her favorite pairs of pants instead of investing in new ones as her weight fluctuates, while turning to ‌fast fashion for the rest of her wardrobe.

US consumers taking weight-loss drugs like Novo Nordisk's Ozempic and Eli Lilly's Mounjaro have turned to cobblers and tailors as they try to save money while shedding pounds, motivated in part by a ​cost-of-living squeeze and rising out-of-pocket costs for the drugs as US employers increasingly drop GLP-1 coverage.

Over the past year, leather repairers have seen a spike in requests for their services due to rapid weight loss — not just for belts, but also for shoe and bag strap adjustments tailored to customers' trimmer bodies.

The uptick in demand for alterations underscores how weight-loss drugs are upending the retail sector, with some corners of the industry well-positioned to benefit while others struggle to adapt. About 11% of US adults are on GLP-1 drugs to lose weight, according to Gallup, forcing millions of consumers to look ‌for affordable ways to revamp their wardrobes.

Cobblers Direct, an online shoe ⁠and handbag repair shop with 25 brick-and-mortar stores in Texas and a nationwide mail-in service, is seeing double-digit year-on-year growth in its belt-shortening business, said CEO Stephen Kelly.

The company, whose around 100 artisans will soon be operating from a new, nearly 30,000-square-foot warehouse in Austin, is now shortening ⁠as much as 500 belts each week, Kelly said.

Customers, he said, have been walking into the stores with five or six belts slung across their shoulder. After getting a few more holes punched in, some have asked to keep the extra flap of leather as a "badge of honor."

"They'll pull their belt out and show how long their belt originally was. And then they tuck it back into their waistline," ​Kelly ​said.

About 80% of GLP-1 users are living in clothes that no longer fit, waiting six months on average ​before buying anything new, according to a survey of more than 700 ‌US adults using weight-loss drugs by telehealth platform Trimi. Jeans are the most disrupted article of clothing, the survey found, with 90% of users lamenting poor fit.

articles.title: José Navarro, fontanero autónomo: "Si me ofrecieran un trabajo asalariado de 4.000 euros al mes, no me iría"
articles.standfirst: El fontanero explica el motivo por el que prefiere ser autónomo
articles.summary: El fontanero explica el motivo por el que prefiere ser autónomo
articles.body: Tener un sueldo fijo y elevado es una de las aspiraciones de muchos trabajadores, especialmente en un contexto en el que el coste de la vida y los gastos cotidianos condicionan cada vez más la economía de los hogares. Sin embargo, no todo el mundo considera que una nómina sea la mejor opción. José Navarro, fontanero autónomo, tiene claro que no cambiaría su situación laboral por un empleo por cuenta ajena, ni siquiera si le ofrecieran cobrar 4.000 euros al mes. Así lo explicó en una entrevista en el pódcast 'Sector Oficios', en la que repasó su trayectoria profesional y las razones por las que decidió dedicarse a la fontanería. "Ser autónomo no es fácil, pero a mí me encanta. De hecho, si a mí me ofrecieran hoy un trabajo asalariado y me pagaran 4.000 euros al mes no me iría", afirmó. Su decisión no responde a que considere que trabajar por cuenta propia le proporcione necesariamente unos ingresos superiores. El propio Navarro matizó que rechazaría esa oferta por otros motivos, relacionados principalmente con la posibilidad de organizar su jornada y disponer de su tiempo. "Prefiero la libertad de poder trabajar hasta la hora que quiera o de coger un día libre cuando quiera", explicó el fontanero. Para él, esa autonomía es uno de los principales atractivos de su actividad y una ventaja que no se puede valorar únicamente comparando dos salarios. Trabajar como autónomo, no obstante, también implica asumir responsabilidades que en un empleo por cuenta ajena suelen recaer en la empresa. La organización de los trabajos, la elaboración de presupuestos, los desplazamientos, los gastos profesionales y la gestión de la actividad forman parte de las obligaciones de quienes trabajan por su cuenta. Navarro conoce esas dificultades, pero asegura que no se arrepiente de la decisión que tomó. Su trayectoria profesional pasó por otros sectores antes de centrarse en la fontanería. Anteriormente, trabajó como albañil y también estuvo vinculado durante años al sector de la automoción. Su testimonio también conecta con uno de los retos del mercado laboral: la disponibilidad de profesionales cualificados en determinados oficios. La fontanería y otras actividades relacionadas con la construcción requieren formación y experiencia, mientras que el envejecimiento de parte de la población ocupada plantea dificultades para garantizar el relevo generacional.

articles.standfirst: La electricidad se encarece notablemente este jueves
articles.summary: La electricidad se encarece notablemente este jueves
articles.body: Hoy jueves, el precio medio de la electricidad se sitúa en 155,63 €/MWh, un incremento de 8,66 € respecto al día anterior, que cerró en 146,97 €/MWh. Esta tendencia al alza plantea la necesidad de analizar las horas más caras y más baratas del día, para optimizar el consumo eléctrico y reducir costes. Los precios de la luz alcanzan su punto más alto en las horas de mayor consumo, concentrándose especialmente en la franja entre las 08:00 y las 21:00. Durante este periodo, se evidencian picos notables, siendo la hora más cara de todas la de 08:00 a 09:00 con un coste de 256.07 €/MWh, seguida de 19:00 a 20:00 con 242.32 €/MWh y 20:00 a 21:00 con 245.28 €/MWh. La tendencia muestra que las franjas horarias más costosas se agrupan principalmente en la mañana y al final de la tarde, lo cual puede derivarse del incremento en la demanda eléctrica. La electricidad es más barata en las horas nocturnas y del mediodía, lo que presenta una clara oportunidad de ahorro para los consumidores. Las franjas horarias más relevantes incluyen desde las 12:00 hasta las 15:00, donde se registran precios excepcionalmente bajos, comenzando con 3.35 €/MWh a las 12:00 y alcanzando 0.4 €/MWh a las 15:00. Este periodo de aproximadamente tres horas representa la ventana más amplia de precios bajos en la jornada, contrastando fuertemente con las horas pico, que superan los 200 €/MWh. El análisis de las 24 franjas horarias revela una notable concentración de precios extremadamente bajos en la franja del mediodía, donde se registraron precios por debajo de 3,50 €/MWh durante varias horas. Este fenómeno es especialmente relevante para los consumidores, ya que pueden aprovechar estos momentos más económicos para realizar su consumo eléctrico, optimizando así su factura mensual.

articles.body: Tata Sons and Tata Trusts are in talks with insurance companies about cover for possible legal claims arising from their dispute over the future of the $185 billion Tata Group.Executives from both sides want to know how much of their legal costs would be covered under directors and officers liability insurance if the dispute goes to court, according to people familiar with the matter cited by Bloomberg.Possible claims could come from minority shareholders seeking compensation for losses linked to the boardroom dispute or from regulatory action.Tata AIG General Insurance Company Ltd. has issued insurance policies to both Tata Sons and Tata Trusts, the people said. The policies also allow the two sides to file claims against each other over valuation losses. Other directors on the Tata Sons board overruled his objections, leaving the group's leadership increasingly divided.The Tata Sons board wants to proceed with a public listing in line with guidance from India's banking regulator for systemically important shadow lenders. The holding company, in its current structure, would fall within this category.Noel Tata has opposed the move, arguing that a listing would dilute the philanthropic mission of Tata Trusts, expose the group to market volatility and undermine a governance model that has lasted a century.The disagreement over leadership has added to the tensions. Tata Trusts has called the board's decision to reappoint Chandrasekaran an “illegal” move.Although neither side has taken the other to court, both have engaged prominent lawyers ahead of a possible legal confrontation.Insurance could cover legal costsDirectors and officers liability insurance is designed to protect senior executives against personal financial losses if they face lawsuits arising from their professional responsibilities. The cover can also meet legal fees and other costs incurred by an organisation in connection with such proceedings.The ongoing discussions are focused on understanding the scope of this protection should the Tata Sons-Tata Trusts dispute lead to litigation, including potential claims involving shareholders or regulators.The insurance arrangements could become relevant if the disagreement results in legal proceedings, although no claims under the policies have been filed so far, the people familiar with the matter said.The Tata Group has previously used insurance coverage to pay legal expenses during a major corporate dispute. articles.title: On Main Street, Goldman Sachs makes a big bet on AI
articles.summary: Goldman Sachs partners with OpenAI, Google, Meta and Anthropic to boost AI adoption among small businesses.
articles.body: Artificial intelligence is already a huge business for Wall Street. But how is it playing on Main Street? Goldman Sachs, as part of a philanthropic effort, is spending big in an attempt to help ensure smaller employers get in on it. The bank announced Thursday that it has launched the Small Business AI Institute as part of a $500 million expansion of its 10,000 Small Businesses, a program geared toward educating and supporting entrepreneurs. It said it would partner with Google, Anthropic, OpenAI and Meta to provide AI training and tools to small businesses. “You’ve got to embrace new technology always, because if you’re not embracing it, trying to figure out how it can make your businesses better, there’s a real chance that you can fall behind,” Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon said in an exclusive interview for NBC News’ Business in America series. It’s a pivotal moment for the AI wave and its financial backers, including Goldman. The technology is broadly available to consumers, and U.S. economic growth increasingly depends on the buildup of data centers. “We believe AI will create the greatest boom in entrepreneurship and small businesses that the world has ever seen,” Sam Altman, CEO and co-founder of OpenAI, said in an announcement from Goldman Sachs. “This is an incredible moment for anyone with an idea for a new endeavor because the gap between imagining it and bringing it to life is getting much smaller.” Yet the growth that AI is already driving has also helped push up prices for inflation-weary Americans. Anger at data centers is a rare point of bipartisan agreement among voters, and the midterm elections are days away. In the finance world, critics say AI is an investment bubble that could burst and potentially wipe out companies and jobs. Cracks are forming in the AI trade in markets after Big Tech firms drove much of stocks’ recent surge to record highs. Goldman Sachs, like much of Wall Street, is in the thick of it all. The bank’s share price has approximately tripled over the past three years while AI-related companies pushed the stock market to record highs. Goldman helped lead the much-ballyhooed, record-breaking initial public offering for Elon Musk’s SpaceX, which counts xAI and Grok among its core businesses. Goldman is also reportedly working on the IPO of Anthropic, the startup behind the AI chatbot Claude. “There is going to be a lot of financing to do,” Solomon said last week on an earnings call, “and we’re going to be in the middle of that.” Goldman and other big firms are counting on small businesses, which make up more than 90% of all U.S. companies and drive most of America’s job growth, to buy in. It won’t be easy getting everyone on board, though. A recent NBC News poll found that 79% of respondents believe the government isn’t doing enough to regulate AI use. Sixty-seven percent disapprove of how President Donald Trump is handling the technology. Trump has said he favors lax AI regulation from the government. Meanwhile, some small businesses that already embraced AI have faced backlash from the public, including restaurants that used AI-generated images of food that critics denounced as “slop.” Still, according to Goldman, entrepreneurs are adopting the technology at a fast clip. A survey this year of more than 2,400 graduates of the company’s small business program found that 86% of respondents were using AI in their businesses, up from just 56% in 2024. Rechelle Balanzat, founder of the laundry services app Juliette and an alumna of the 10,000 Small Businesses program, told NBC News she sees AI as a tool to help her gin up more business with limited resources. “I really treat my AI as my consigliere,” Balanzat said. “They are not there to replace your accountant and lawyer. They are not there to replace humans. However, it does help prep me to have much more meaningful questions when I am meeting with my accountant and with my lawyer.” Despite the widespread use of AI among the Goldman program alumni, just 15% of them said they had fully integrated AI into their core operations, according to Goldman. Mike DiMarino, who heads Linda Tool in Brooklyn, New York, was part of the inaugural class of Goldman’s program in 2010. The company makes precision machine components for the military and aerospace industries, and DiMarino thinks AI can help with planning, management and processes. “I’m sure there’s a lot more it can do that I don’t know yet,” he said. But DiMarino is also cautious about how Linda Tool uses the technology, especially given how much sensitive information the company handles for its work in defense, aerospace and manufacturing. His concerns mirror broader cybersecurity fears about AI. In July, a swarm of about 700 AI agents created by OpenAI hacked into the open-source platform Hugging Face. Last month, Google said Chinese hackers are using AI to automate their attacks. In addition to the security risks, company leaders are also increasingly raising concerns about the cost of AI, especially relative to its concrete impact on the bottom line. After spending on AI tokens exploded in the past year, companies from Uber to Microsoft to Meta have all taken steps to limit or re-evaluate how their employees use AI compute power. Americans are also concerned about what AI will do to the job market. A recent Gallup Poll found that a growing number of workers are worried that technology will make their jobs obsolete. Small businesses employ fewer people than large firms, which makes their workforces especially vulnerable to potential losses. Balanzat and DiMarino told NBC News they want to use AI to support employees at their businesses, not replace them. “Machines are expensive,” DiMarino said. “People are priceless.”

articles.title: India’s private capex pipeline rises 39% to Rs 99.7 lakh crore, UBI flags risks
articles.summary: India’s planned private sector investments touched Rs 99.7 lakh crore in September 2026, with the pipeline expanding 39% over a year.
articles.body: India’s planned private sector investments touched Rs 99.7 lakh crore in September 2026, with the pipeline expanding 39% over a year. However, the sharp rise in project costs has not been matched by a similar increase in the number of projects, raising concerns about how widely the investment recovery is spread across the economy, according to a report by Union Bank of India (UBI) Research.The pipeline has grown 87% in two years, but the number of projects has increased by only 18%. This suggests that larger projects, rather than a broad increase in investment activity, have accounted for much of the growth.The report said, “The capex cycle is firmly aligned with Viksit Bharat 2047 aspirations,” while cautioning that the recovery was not yet broad-based.The scale of the increase is evident from the addition to announced project costs. These rose by Rs 46.4 lakh crore over the past two years, compared with just Rs 7 lakh crore added in the eight years up to March 2022. The overall pipeline is now 4.1 times its March 2014 level.Two sectors account for most of the increaseIT-enabled services (ITES) and conventional power were the biggest contributors to the latest annual rise, together accounting for 87% of the net increase. ITES added Rs 16.8 lakh crore to the pipeline, while conventional power contributed Rs 7.6 lakh crore.The ITES pipeline alone jumped from Rs 2.2 lakh crore to Rs 18.9 lakh crore in a year, covering 160 projects.Looking at the outstanding pipeline, manufacturing and electricity together made up 74% of the total. Manufacturing projects accounted for Rs 41.3 lakh crore, while electricity projects stood at Rs 32.2 lakh crore.The services sector recorded the highest annual growth rate, surging 347% to Rs 21.9 lakh crore.Five states dominate investment growthMaharashtra continued to lead as a destination for announced private investments, with projects worth Rs 28.6 lakh crore. This represented around 29% of the total pipeline.The concentration was also visible in the distribution of fresh additions. Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Odisha and Uttar Pradesh together accounted for 94% of the pipeline’s annual increase.UBI Research flagged this concentration, along with the disparity between the growth in announced project costs and the number of projects, as risks for the next phase of the investment cycle.Power investment gap raises execution concernsThe report also highlighted a substantial difference between planned investments in power generation and transmission. articles.title: Apple’s Cash Flow Machine Makes It Investors’ Favorite AI Hedge
articles.summary: It’s become one of the most reliable trades in the stock market as sentiment toward artificial intelligence swings wildly: Whatever AI stocks do, Apple Inc....
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- It's become one of the most reliable trades in the stock market as sentiment toward artificial intelligence swings wildly: Whatever AI stocks do, Apple Inc. does the opposite.

The iPhone maker's stock is up 27% in 2026, making it the biggest contributor to the S&P 500 Index's 13% climb. It's also by far the best performer among the Magnificent Seven technology giants this year, a stark reversal from 2025, when its 8% gain put it near the bottom of the group.

The reason for the divergence is fairly simple. While most mega-cap tech companies are spending wildly on AI infrastructure, Apple is largely sitting it out and instead focusing on what it historically does best, creating products that get consumers buzzing, like its new foldable iPhone Duo. With Wall Street's view toward AI capital expenditures seemingly in constant flux, the company's shares have become investors' preferred method for staying in Big Tech while avoiding some of the group's ups and downs.

"Apple is a very liquid hedge against AI volatility, and it's a great position to have if you're starting to get worried about AI but still want tech exposure," said Jordan McCall, senior portfolio manager at Russell Investments, which has $418 billion in assets and owns the company's shares in multiple portfolios. "Apple is a flight to safety when the market gets nervous."

Investors are searching for safety because sentiment around AI is shifting so quickly. Shares of the big spenders like Microsoft Corp., Amazon.com Inc., Alphabet Inc. and Meta Platforms Inc., and the chipmakers at the heart of AI infrastructure, rise and fall as Wall Street debates when and if the hundreds of billions in capital expenditures will pay off in a big way. Apple has an increasingly negative correlation to semiconductor stocks and often moves in the opposite direction of its mega-cap peers.

The dynamic was apparent last week, when concerns about cloud computing provider CoreWeave Inc.'s debt spurred widespread selling of AI stocks. The Philadelphia Stock Exchange Semiconductor index, better known as the SOX, tumbled more than 11%, marking its worst week since April 2025, while an index of Magnificent Seven stocks sank 3.1%. Apple, meanwhile, rose 2% as the company said demand for the Duo was "nothing short of extraordinary."

articles.title: Oil jumps on escalating Middle East conflict
articles.summary: By Seher Dareen and Siyi Liu LONDON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Brent prices rose to their highest since May on Thursday after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia st...
articles.body:
LONDON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - Brent prices rose to their highest since May on Thursday after more Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia stoked concerns over a broader escalation of conflict and further ‌disruptions to crude oil supplies from the world's key exporting region.

Brent crude futures climbed $3.35 or 3.08%, to $112.17 a barrel ‌by 0818 GMT, the highest since May 18. They hit $112.55 a barrel earlier in the session.

US West Texas Intermediate crude gained $2.68, or 2.76%, to $99.83.

"Efforts to mitigate tensions, ​both in Ukraine and the Middle East, lack credibility ... reports of Middle East crude oil exports exceeding pre-conflict levels are more than countered by attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz and the Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia and on its oil infrastructure," PVM Oil analyst Tamas Varga said.

"No de-escalation is anticipated until the US midterm elections, which should keep oil prices elevated."

Morgan Stanley analysts estimated in ‌a note that Middle East crude oil ⁠exports were around 17 million barrels per day last week.

The US State Department has ordered some diplomats and family members to leave its missions in Saudi Arabia and plans to withdraw family members from ⁠a number of other US missions in the Middle East, US officials told Reuters.

Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis struck several targets in Saudi Arabia on Wednesday with at least one person killed and eight more wounded at a civilian airport in Dammam, and two people killed in a drone ​attack on ​a Saudi oil field.

Explosions were also heard in Sirik in southern Iran, ​Iranian media reported on Wednesday, saying the nature and ‌origin of the explosions were unknown.

Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy said on Thursday that four vessels involved in illegal oil transfers in the northern Gulf were simultaneously hit and caught fire after being tracked by its forces on Wednesday.

The IRGC added that three more vessels collided with mines west of the Strait of Hormuz, and warned the US military that continued provocations could lead to a wider response against its regional bases.

Supply disruption continued to affect global inventories. A valve on an oil pipeline running ‌from Libya's Hamada and Tahara oilfields to Zawiya port has been shut, ​leading to a reduction in production at both fields, the head of the ​National Oil Corporation told Reuters.

Seeking to contain prices that ​have surged on diesel shortages due to the US-Israeli war with Iran and the Russian war in ‌Ukraine, the Trump administration is offering to loan up ​to nearly a third of the ​1-million-barrel US emergency heating oil reserve.

However, a $9.89 billion legal charge pushed operating income down 37 per cent despite a 26 per cent increase in overall revenue.The company's revenue reached $64.60 billion in the quarter ended September 30, compared with $51.24 billion in the same period last year. Net income stood at $2.71 billion a year earlier, while diluted earnings per share rose to $3.83 from $1.05.Advertising remained the biggest contributor to Meta's revenue, bringing in $63.06 billion, up 26 per cent from a year ago. Total costs and expenses climbed 68 per cent to $51.61 billion, reflecting, among other expenses, a $9.89 billion charge tied to an agreement with 52 US state attorneys general to resolve litigation concerning teen mental health and social media.Meta said that excluding this charge, operating income would have been $22.88 billion. articles.title: Wall Street's big CoreWeave stock bear is now even more bearish
articles.summary: CoreWeave continues to be a hotly debated stock.
articles.body:
So much for a bullish tone from Elon Musk on AI demand during his SpaceX ( SPCX ) earnings call, arresting the slide in CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and other neocloud stocks.

At least as seen through the eyes of one of Wall Street's biggest CoreWeave bears.

Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei slashed her price target on the stock to $51 from $74 on Thursday and maintained an Underperform rating.

"We caught a lot of hate when we initiated on CRWV with a $56 price target seven months ago. Today, it's a lot harder to find bulls—certainly some of them just don't call us anymore, but there seems to be more broad acceptance of the challenges of this business model. Could this turn around? Maybe: it's a wildly volatile, momentum-driven stock, but barring major moves, the fundamentals are probably stuck," Rezaei said.

If there is any positive for the CRWV bulls, Rezaei doesn't think the stock is headed to $0.

"We do not believe CRWV is a 0—they still have a large backlog, line of sight to powered shell delivery, and while we don't think the contracts are super attractive, they're not underwater. Whether Nvidia ( NVDA ) will step in is meatier; we think they would intervene in a true downside. Doesn't necessarily re-energize the stock, but raises the floor," she added.

CoreWeave's stock has been torched in October to the tune of 28%. Shares lost 6% in pre-market trading today.

The company's corporate bonds across maturities continued to be dumped amid fears of an AI slowdown and its implications for the company's precarious balance sheet. That has triggered a subsequent sharp sell-off in the stock.

The rise in yields on CoreWeave's bonds even spurred Elon Musk to post "Yikes" on X in response to a post by venture capitalist Chamath Palihapitiya last week.

Meanwhile, in a new report, Gartner forecast that by 2030, "cost pressure and a lack of a differentiating business model will force over 80% of neocloud providers to cease independent operations."

Brian Sozzi is Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor, host of the Sozzi Unleashed morning show and the Power Players with Brian Sozzi podcast, and a member of Yahoo Finance's editorial leadership team.

articles.title: Copper Declines as Tech-Stock Selloff Dulls Appetite for Risk
articles.summary: Copper fell with other industrial metals, as a selloff in AI-related stocks sapped risk appetite across global markets.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Copper ( HG=F ) fell with other industrial metals, as a selloff in AI-related stocks sapped risk appetite across global markets.

The red metal slipped as much as 0.7% to $14,260 a ton on the London Metal Exchange. Asian shares slid after earnings from major tech companies failed to reassure investors about the durability of the artificial intelligence trade. Copper has benefited from that boom because of its use in data centers and power infrastructure.

Its retreat from last month's record high of $14,875 a ton has also been fueled by doubts over whether the US will impose a tariff on refined copper as President Donald Trump approaches the midpoint of his second term. The prospect of a levy has drawn vast amounts of the metal into US warehouses this year, squeezing supplies elsewhere.

"There is still a great deal of uncertainty around next year's copper supply-demand balance," said Zhenting Zhou, a trader at Hangzhou Chenglian Industrial Co. "Mine supply should improve, US import demand is likely to ease, and China's scrap-copper availability should also recover. There isn't much upside risk for copper," he said.

Still, some concerns remain around supply disruptions. Workers at Canada's largest copper mine, Teck Resources Ltd.'s Highland Valley Copper operation, are threatening to strike as early as Saturday, in the latest sign of labor tensions prompted by near-record prices that have emboldened employees to seek a greater share of profits.

Copper was 0.4% lower at $14,294.50 a ton on the LME as of 11 a.m. in Shanghai. Aluminum declined 0.6% to $3,023.50, while nickel gave up 1% after surging 3.7% in the prior session on the prospect of coordinated output cuts by Chinese producers in Indonesia.

Iron ore fell as much as 1.7% to $89.45 a ton in Singapore, the lowest in almost two years, before paring losses.

articles.title: The Live Nation Empire That Music Fans Hate is at Risk of a Break Up
articles.summary: Critics say the music giant at the center of an antitrust lawsuit is crowding out independent venues — and making it harder for new acts to break through.
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- The Crowbar nightclub of Tampa, Florida never looked like much outside: a squat building with painted-over windows in a neighborhood where feral chickens roam brick streets.

Inside was where the magic happened. For 20 years, Crowbar's single, 300-person room served as a place to hear unknown artists before they broke or popular acts offering more intimate shows. Musicians as different as rock band OK Go, country's Kenny Chesney and indie-pop singer Chappell Roan graced its stage. A generation of local rappers honed their skills there.

On July 31, Crowbar closed its doors for the last time, beset by rising costs and the elephant in any discussion about concerts in the US: Live Nation Entertainment Inc. The colossus — which owns arenas and clubs, runs the nation's biggest ticketing service and manages musicians' careers — plans to build its own venue nearby. For Crowbar's final show, rapper Talib Kweli flew down from New York City, with local hip hop artists joining him onstage.

Across the country, some 480 independent venues and 240 music festivals have shut since 2020, with 160 shuttering so far this year, according to the National Independent Venue Association, a trade group for the industry. While the Covid-19 pandemic and surging inflation each played a role, so has the market power of Live Nation, according to Crowbar owner Tom DeGeorge and other independents. They struggle to compete against a $40 billion company that can steer artists to play one venue and avoid others while exerting significant control over ticket pricing through its Ticketmaster subsidiary.

This year, the Trump administration agreed to settle a monopoly case against Live Nation weeks after the company's CEO met with the president. The company denies any political interference. Displeased with the deal, a group of states fought on and, in April, won a landmark jury verdict that the company illegally monopolized live events. Now, those states want a federal judge to take the rare step of ordering a corporate breakup. Independent club owners and many musicians argue it's the only way to bring balance back to the market.

"If Live Nation wasn't the monopoly they were, I think all of our independent venues would have the ability to thrive much more," DeGeorge said in an interview. "When you have one entity that comes in that controls the entire ocean, nobody else gets to swim."

articles.title: Netflix is losing viewers — but they're still subscribed
articles.summary: People aren't leaving the service, but they aren't watching it enthusiastically, either.
articles.body:
Netflix ( NFLX ) has a unique problem: subscription zombies.

The company is seeing sagging engagement in the US , while also claiming an industry-low churn rate. People aren't leaving the service, but they aren't watching it enthusiastically, either.

If the company's stock price — down 30% this year — is any indication , investors are fed up. But the steep fall from prior highs is, given the right insights and conviction, another buying opportunity.

That's how analysts at Deutsche Bank see things. In a note published Wednesday, Bryan Kraft made the case for buying the dip.

After the company reported third quarter earnings, Netflix shares fell to their lowest level in more than two years as the streaming giant missed estimates on the current quarter's revenue outlook and the full-year ad revenue forecast.

As management acknowledged there's room for its US business to do better , Kraft took a contrarian take.

Netflix viewing continues to grow outside the US, and in every region churn is down compared to last year, in every region, despite recent price hikes, he said.

"We found management's commentary on churn, international viewing, new content leadership, and their long-term growth outlook all pretty encouraging," he said.

The market has fixated on sagging time spent watching and a lackluster slate of content. But Kraft believes this stems from a weaker lineup compared to last year, rather than a deeper decline in quality.

Netflix's stock market struggle and its engagement problem both arrive with a dose of irony. After all, Paramount's ( SKYD ) stated justification for pursuing Warner Bros. was to get big enough to compete with Netflix. But Netflix is looking less like an indomitable tech giant and more like a beleaguered studio struggling to convince American audiences that it isn't a slop factory.

Netflix has a reputation for being the comfort streamer — the limitless provider of pleasant background noise while you fold laundry or try to fall asleep. That has value, of course. But YouTube gives you that for free. And TikTok and Instagram's Reels spare you the mental load of having to choose what to put on.

The recent executive shakeups also suggest that Netflix had ceded, or perhaps never really went after, the sought-after TV shows and movies that people associate with Apple TV and HBO Max.

But Kraft said that the growth outlook for Netflix remains healthy, even with some deceleration next year. There's member growth, price increases, more box office revenue, and advertising to support a more bullish thesis.

articles.title: Tesla is spending less now, but the bill is coming later: Chart of the Day
articles.summary: Tesla cut $5 billion from this year's spending plan. It also told investors the bill is going up from here.
articles.body:
Tesla cut $5 billion from this year's spending plan. It also told investors the bill is going up from here.

On Wednesday, Tesla ( TSLA ) lowered its 2026 capital spending guidance to about $20 billion from $25 billion. The cut came after a quarter in which it spent $4.73 billion, about $3.2 billion less than analysts expected, according to Bloomberg estimates. The lighter spending helped Tesla generate $1.53 billion in free cash flow , when Wall Street had braced for it to burn nearly $5 billion.

"Our capex for the next few years would continue to expand as we add more robotaxi fleet, we expand our production capacity for Optimus, install manufacturing capacity for solar, purchase additional SI compute infrastructure, and build a semiconductor fab," Chief Financial Officer Vaibhav Taneja said on the company's earnings call.

Tesla also lined up the ability to borrow up to $30 billion to support that growth, though Taneja said it doesn't plan to tap the money this year. Shares fell 2% after hours following a 3.4% gain in the regular session.

Through three quarters, Tesla has spent about $13 billion. The new plan leaves roughly $7 billion for the fourth quarter.

That would still be a record, about 20% above the $5.8 billion Tesla spent in the second quarter. But it's well short of what the old plan required: nearly $12 billion in one quarter, more than the $8.5 billion Tesla spent in all of 2025.

The biggest project is just getting started. Musk said Terafab, the chip plant Tesla is building with SpaceX, will need tens of billions of dollars in equipment through early 2028 and likely more than $100 billion over the long term. The two companies still have to work out who pays for what. Real production isn't expected until late 2028.

Spending on other projects is already ramping. Tesla expects to have 400 megawatts of AI training compute running by year-end. It has started Optimus robot production in Fremont, Calif., and is building a second, larger robot factory in Austin.

"We're definitely, as I say in Vegas, betting on the come," Musk said.

articles.title: Tesla stock slips despite Q3 earnings beat, better-than-expected capex spend
articles.summary: Tesla reported Q3 earnings after the bell.
articles.body:
Tesla ( TSLA ) reported better-than-expected third quarter earnings, with its free cash flow and capex spending coming in ahead of Wall Street estimates.

Tesla reported Q3 revenue of $28.05 billion vs. Bloomberg consensus of $28.13 billion. Tesla posted adjusted EPS of $0.48 vs. the $0.44 estimate, with adjusted EBITDA of $3.90 billion vs. $3.66 billion.

Tesla stock fell almost 5% before the bell on Thursday, with Morningstar analyst Seth Goldstein claiming the market was reacting to "capacity constraints in the company's auto and battery growth, which could slow near-term growth."

But that might not be the whole story. Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion vs. an estimated -$4.92 billion, with capital expenditures climbing to $4.732 billion vs. an estimated $7.96 billion for the quarter.

On the earnings call, Tesla updated its full-year capex guidance to $20 billion from $25 billion previously. Tesla CFO Vaibhav Taneja said the savings would come from "managing our capital deployment efficiently, and plan to fund [capex] primarily from our cash flows from operations," he said.

"I think capex is actually ending up being a little lower than we anticipated, but we'll start to become more meaningful next year. And then noticeable in the tens of billions in '28," CEO Elon Musk said on the call.

Roundhill CEO Dave Mazza posits the cutting capex means the Tesla isn't transitioning fast enough to an AI-focused company betting on robotaxis, Optimus robots, and compute.

Tesla revealed its Optimus robot started production at its Fremont factory. "While we will continue to iterate on the hardware and manufacturing process, we have proven that the current manufacturing process for Optimus is suitable for a commercial product," the company said in its earnings release.

"I would expect that it takes us probably at least a year — maybe a little longer — to get to that annualized rate [1 million units], to get to 20,000 units a week," Musk said on the earnings call. Musk added that Tesla may release an Optimus demo video in about a month, stressing that he didn't want the robot's movements to be preplanned.

Regarding its other AI efforts, Tesla said it plans to reach 400 MW of AI training compute by the end of the year. Tesla said its active FSD (full self-driving) subscriptions climbed to 1.74 million.

"The biggest driver of demand is full self-driving," Musk said regarding vehicle sales.

"The Cybercab fleet in Austin has grown by a factor of 10," Musk added while discussing Tesla's robotaxi fleet. He added, "I don't think there's any company in the world that can match our scale with autonomous vehicles."

articles.title: María Cristina Buendía, notaria, sobre la nueva Ley de Propiedad Horizontal: “Si un vecino mayor de 70 años pide un ascensor, la comunidad ya no puede desentenderse”
articles.standfirst: La reforma, que entra en vigor este 23 de octubre, obliga a las comunidades a pedir ayudas para obras de accesibilidad
articles.summary: La reforma, que entra en vigor este 23 de octubre, obliga a las comunidades a pedir ayudas para obras de accesibilidad
articles.body: Las comunidades de propietarios tienen una nueva obligación en el horizonte, y muchas todavía no lo saben. La notaria María Cristina Buendía ha querido advertirlo en un vídeo en redes sociales, en el que explica cómo un cambio legal que entra en vigor esta misma semana puede afectar a la convivencia, y a los gastos, de miles de edificios. “Muy atentas todas las comunidades de propietarios”, avisa. Se refiere a la reforma de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal incluida en la Ley 4/2026, publicada en el BOE el 3 de octubre, que entra en vigor el 23 de octubre de 2026. El cambio afecta a las obras de accesibilidad que pide un vecino con discapacidad o mayor de 70 años. Buendía pone como ejemplo los casos más frecuentes: la instalación de un ascensor o de una rampa. Explica que, si un vecino que cumple esos requisitos solicita estas obras y aporta información sobre las ayudas y subvenciones disponibles en materia de vivienda, “es la comunidad de propietarios la obligada a solicitar estas ayudas”. Y añade: “No puede la junta desentenderse de este trámite”. Hasta ahora, la comunidad no tenía por qué tramitarlas. A partir del 23 de octubre, solicitarlas deja de ser optativo. La segunda novedad tiene que ver con el dinero. Según explica la notaria, si las ayudas realmente concedidas alcanzan el 70% del coste de las obras, ejecutarlas es obligatorio para la comunidad. Hasta ahora ese porcentaje estaba fijado en el 75%. Además, la ley tiene en cuenta las ayudas efectivamente concedidas, no las que la comunidad podría llegar a recibir. Si aun así la comunidad no cumple, Buendía recuerda que ese vecino “puede acudir a un tribunal y ser el juez el que ordene la ejecución” de las obras. Cuando las ayudas concedidas no llegan al 70%, o el coste supera el tope previsto, las obras solo siguen siendo obligatorias si quien las pidió paga la diferencia. La notaria aclara una excepción territorial: la norma no se aplicará en Cataluña, que cuenta con su propia regulación específica en esta materia.
